newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean medical team heads for crash site.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean medical team heads for crash site.

text.p: A 27-member medical team left for Guam on Wednesday to help airlift home South Koreans injured in the crash of a Korean Air Lines (KAL) jumbo jet, Seoul officials said.

The team will accompany home most of the 30 people who survived the crash on Wednesday. KAL Flight 801 left Seoul at 8.22 p.m. (1122 GMT) carrying 254 people and plummeted into a hillside on the Pacific island at 1:15 a.m. (1515 GMT Tuesday).
U.S. officials in Guam said 69 people had been confirmed dead and 155 were missing.
Many of the survivors suffered major burns from a fire that broke out after the crash, KAL officials said.
"The medical team will bring back to Seoul those survivors who are in good enough state to travel," said a KAL spokesman.
The spokesman also said a special flight taking relatives of South Korean passengers had left for Guam.
